t.5.57.2: Having encountered the virtuous character of Sītā, the endeavor of Rāghava has borne fruit, as has the eager zeal of Sugrīva, and my own great leap as well.
t.5.57.1: Hanumān, the son of the Wind, once more set about speaking further words, telling this whole account in full.
t.5.57.3: O bulls among monkeys, the conduct of the noble Sītā is worthy of her; by her austerity she could sustain the worlds, or, if angered, she could even burn them up.
t.5.57.4: That Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, is mighty in every way, for though he touched her, his body was not destroyed by her tapas.
t.5.57.5: A tongue of flame, even when touched by the hand, would not do what the daughter of Janaka, roused and darkened by fierce anger, would do.
t.5.57.6: In the middle of the Aśoka grove of the evil-minded Rāvaṇa, beneath a śiṃśapā tree, the virtuous lady remains in a pitiable state.
t.5.57.7: Surrounded by rākṣasīs and emaciated by grief and anguish, she was lustreless, like a crescent of the moon surrounded by streaks of cloud.
t.5.57.8: Vaidehī gives no thought to Rāvaṇa, proud of his strength; the fair-hipped Jānakī, devoted to her husband, remains steadfast.
t.5.57.10: Clad in that single garment and covered with dust as well, her limbs wasted with grief and anguish, Sītā remains devoted to the welfare of her husband.
t.5.57.9: For the auspicious Vaidehī is devoted to Rāma with her whole being, and her mind rests on Rāma alone, as Paulomī's does on Puraṃdara.
t.5.57.12: Wearing her hair in a single braid, wretched, wholly absorbed in thoughts of her husband, sleeping on the bare ground, her limbs pale and wan, she was like a lotus pond at the coming of winter.
t.5.57.11: Indeed, I saw her there in the grove, in the midst of the rākṣasīs, being threatened again and again by those hideous rākṣasī women.
t.5.57.13: The fawn-eyed lady, who had turned wholly away from Rāvaṇa and had made up her mind to die, was somehow brought to place her trust in me.
t.5.57.14: Then she was spoken to and shown the whole matter, and on hearing of the friendship between Rāma and Sugrīva, she was filled with joy.
t.5.57.15: Her conduct is disciplined and restrained, and her devotion to her husband is supreme.
t.5.57.17: Thus does the illustrious Sītā remain, wholly given over to grief. Whatever must be done here in response, let all of it be carried out.
t.5.57.16: That the great-souled Daśānana does not himself slay Daśagrīva is only because Rāma will be the mere instrument in his death.
